text: Tiba is a payment rail for software that pays people without asking a human to approve every transfer.
The problem is simple. Software can already move money. What it cannot do is decide, safely, when to move it.
The operator console shows the boundary: daily cap, hourly cap, recipients, work orders, and the kill switch.
Every limit here is set once, in advance, by a human. A cap on each payment, caps per hour and per day, and a list of who may be paid at all.
The kill switch belongs to the operator, not the agent. Nothing the agent says can switch it off.
The demo submits two payout paths in the background: one clean delivery and one tampered request.
Behind the scenes two checks are running through GonkaRouter, and they are deliberately given different evidence.
One reads the delivery note the agent supplied. The other reads only our own payer records, and never sees that note.
Every payable amount starts as a registered work order. The AI can match delivery to approved work; it cannot invent a new payment.
You can try all four cases here. A clean delivery note, a prompt injection, an inflated amount, and an unknown work order.
The first one should pay. The other three should be refused. That is the product.
Both checks must name the same work order and the same amount. If they disagree, Tiba refuses rather than split the difference.
The ledger records both outcomes. A clean path becomes paid, while the adversarial path is refused.
Here both outcomes sit side by side. Two USDC paid to Ali, and one refusal, in the same list.
The refusal is the row that matters. Channel A read nine hundred and ninety nine USDC. Channel B read two.
The red row shows the refusal reason, and its public receipt shows both channels. The model reading the evidence can be fooled, but the separate payer-record check disagrees, so Tiba refuses.
The receipt is public. Anyone can open it and see which channel said what, and the Gonka request ID behind each one.
The paid row includes a public digest. The recipient can inspect the chain record instead of trusting our database.
Both outcomes stay in the ledger as records, with request IDs, reason codes, and receipt links.
The proof is narrow on purpose: testnet only, SUI as a stand-in asset, GonkaRouter doing the verification.
Software does the work. The human holds the line.
